deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous folio). Dedekind's notation: for rationals x,y,..., [x,y,...] is the positive generator of the Z-module x Z + y Z + ... (the 'g.g.Th.' of rationals). 'x ≡ 0 (mod μ)' means x ∈ μZ, also for rational μ. A sum of brackets is the gcd of all entries.

The data are rationals a_r, b_r (r = 1..n), with
- 𝔄 = Σ[a_r] + [1],
- 𝔅 = Σ[b_r] + [1],
- ℭ = Σ[a_r b_s − b_r a_s] + Σ[a_r] + Σ[b_r] + [1].

The previous folio defines positive integers a, b, c by 𝔄 = aℭ, 𝔅 = bℭ, ℭ = c𝔄𝔅. Hence ℭ = 1/(abc), 𝔄 = 1/(bc), 𝔅 = 1/(ac). Integers a', a'_r and b'' are chosen with
- 1/(bc) = a' + Σ a_r a'_r,
- b''/(ac) = Σ b_r a'_r.

The goal is to describe all solutions of the n+2 congruences a_r u + b_r v ≡ 0, u ≡ 0, v ≡ 0 (mod 1). This is the lattice L = {(u,v) ∈ Z²: a_r u + b_r v ∈ Z for all r}. Dedekind wants an explicit Z-basis of L and a unimodular change of variables.

(A) Upper block: an exploratory, partly abandoned attempt.
- Put m/a = Σ[b_r − a_r bb''/a] + [bb''/a], so m = Σ[ab_r − bb''a_r] + [bb'']. m is an integer, because b_r − a_r bb''/a ∈ (1/a)Z (proved on the previous folio) and bb'' ∈ Z.
- Identity: (ab_r − bb''a_r)a_s − (ab_s − bb''a_s)a_r = a(b_r a_s − a_r b_s).
- Write ab_r − bb''a_r = m c_r with c_r ∈ Z. Since a_s ∈ (1/(bc))Z, the left side is ≡ 0 mod m/(bc). Hence b_r a_s − a_r b_s ≡ 0 mod m/(abc).
- From bb'' ≡ 0 mod m: b'' ≡ 0 mod m/b and mod 1. With [1, m/b] = 1/p this gives b'' ≡ 0 mod lcm(1, m/b) = mp/b. (Here p is a temporary symbol, reused later with another meaning.)
- bc·b_r = bc(b_r − a_r bb''/a) + (bca_r)(bb''/a) ≡ 0 mod m/a, using bca_r ∈ Z. Hence b_r ≡ 0 mod m/(abc).
- acb_r − bca_r b'' = c·m c_r ≡ 0 mod mc.
- Right column: m Σ c_r a'_r = Σ(ab_r − bb''a_r)a'_r = a·b''/(ac) − bb''(1/(bc) − a') = a'bb''. So Σ c_r a'_r = a'bb''/m.
- Text: every common divisor of b'' and c divides all acb_r (which are integers, ≡ bca_r b'' mod c). It also divides ac·1. Since gcd(acb_r, ac) = ac𝔅 = 1, it divides 1. Hence [b'', c] = 1, i.e. a''b'' + cc'' = 1, and therefore [a'', c''] = 1.
- Multiplying by a'': acb_r a'' ≡ bca_r (mod c). Summing against a'_r gives the check a''b'' − 1 + bca' ≡ 0, i.e. a''b'' ≡ 1 (mod c).
- a''(ab_r − ba_r b'') = (ab_r a'' − ba_r) + bca_r c''.
- 1 = bca' + Σ bca_r a'_r and b'' = Σ acb_r a'_r, so cc'' = 1 − a''b'' = bca' + Σ(bca_r − acb_r a'')a'_r.

(B) Lower block (marked 9): the decisive argument.
- New variables: w_r = a_r u + b_r v, p = Σ w_r a'_r + a'u = u/(bc) + b''v/(ac), q = v/a.
- Then w_r − bca_r p = (b_r − bb''a_r/a)v and u − bcp = −bb''v/a.
- Define 𝔇 = Σ[b_r − (bb''/a)a_r] + [bb''/a] + [1].
- 𝔇 ≡ 0 mod 1/a. Indeed b_r − (bb''/a)a_r = bc{a'b_r + Σ_s(b_r a_s − a_r b_s)a'_s}, with bcb_r ∈ (1/a)Z and bc(b_r a_s − a_r b_s) ∈ bcℭZ = (1/a)Z. Also bb''/a and 1 lie in (1/a)Z.
- Conversely, each of the following is ≡ 0 mod 𝔇:
  - bc(b_r a_s − a_r b_s) = bca_s(b_r − …a_r) − bca_r(b_s − …a_s),
  - bcb_r = bc(b_r − …) + bca_r·bb''/a,
  - bca_r and bc, which are integers.
- So bc·ℭ = 1/a ≡ 0 mod 𝔇. Together: 𝔇 = 1/a. Equivalently gcd(m, a) = 1 for the m of (A).
- Bézout: there are integers h_r, h', h'' with Σ(b_r − bb''a_r/a)h_r − h'bb''/a + h'' = 1/a.
- Multiply by v: q = v/a = Σ(w_r − bca_r p)h_r + (u − bcp)h' + h''v = Σ w_r h_r − bc(Σ a_r h_r + h')(Σ w_r a'_r + a'u) + h'u + h''v.
- So q = Σ b'_r w_r + b'u + c'v with integers [my naming of the explicit values]:
  - b'_r = h_r − bc(Σa_s h_s + h')a'_r,
  - b' = h' − bc(Σa_s h_s + h')a',
  - c' = h''.

(C) Result, boxed on the right.
- w_r = bca_r p + (ab_r − bb''a_r)q,
- u = b(cp − b''q),
- v = aq,
- p = Σ a'_r w_r + a'u,
- q = Σ b'_r w_r + b'u + c'v.

All coefficients are integers. So (u, v, w_r) integral ⇔ (p, q) integral. L has Z-basis (bc, 0), (−bb'', a), a Hermite-type triangular basis, and [Z²:L] = abc = 1/ℭ.

(D) Bottom lines: consistency check by substituting the first three formulas into the last two.
- p-equation: coefficients 1 = bc(Σa_r a'_r + a') and 0 = Σ(ab_r − bb''a_r)a'_r − a'bb''.
- q-equation: 0 = Σ a_r b'_r + b' and 1 = Σ(ab_r − bb''a_r)b'_r − bb'b'' + c'a = aΣ b_r b'_r + ac'. The last step uses Σ a_r b'_r = −b'.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors found; all identities check.
Notational overload: p is first used for [1, m/b] = 1/p in block (A), then later as the new variable p = Σ w_r a'_r + a'u.
Block (A) is exploratory. The line of reasoning with m and c_r is not brought to a conclusion on this page. Its useful content, gcd(m,a) = 1, is obtained instead via 𝔇 = 1/a in block (B).
Claim '[a'',c''] = 1' is correct but trivial (it follows from a''b'' + cc'' = 1); it is not used afterwards.
Implicit facts used without comment: bca_r ∈ Z, acb_r ∈ Z, bcb_r ∈ (1/a)Z, and bc(b_r a_s − a_r b_s) ∈ (1/a)Z. All follow from 𝔄 = 1/(bc), 𝔅 = 1/(ac), ℭ = 1/(abc).

results.what: For rationals a_r, b_r, the lattice of integer (u,v) with all a_r u + b_r v integral has the explicit basis u = b(cp − b''q), v = aq, with index abc = 1/ℭ. Here ℭ is the gcd of 1, the a_r, the b_r and the 2×2 minors a_r b_s − b_r a_s. The construction is an explicit unimodular substitution between (w_r, u, v) and (p, q).
results.modern_name: Hermite normal form of a rank-2 lattice / dual lattice; index of a module given by the gcd of maximal minors (determinantal divisors)
results.usually_credited_to: Hermite (1851) for normal forms; H.J.S. Smith (1861) and Frobenius (1879) for determinantal divisors; Dedekind's own module theory (Supplement XI, 1871–1894) for the index of modules

results.what: 𝔇 = Σ[b_r − (bb''/a)a_r] + [bb''/a] + [1] equals 1/a, giving a Bézout relation used to express q integrally.
results.modern_name: gcd computation in a Z-module of Q / Bézout identity

results.what: gcd(b'', c) = 1, derived from the gcd structure 𝔄, 𝔅, ℭ.
results.modern_name: coprimality lemma in an elementary-divisor computation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful hands-on computation of a basis (Hermite normal form) for a rank-2 lattice defined by rational congruences, with index equal to the inverse gcd of minors. It fits squarely within Dedekind's well-known theory of modules and their indices. The particular explicit formulas are an unpublished working detail, not a new result.
